newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Late South African bonds slipped as a soft bearish trend crept into the market ahead of expectations of higher credit and money supply numbers due out at 1500 GMT.
Traders said lower U.S. Treasuries and a wobbly rand were also driving the negative sentiment.
The big event of the day was the release of April money supply and credit numbers although some traders said it was possible the figures had already been discounted in the market.
At 1616 GMT the R150 stock had edged higher to 15.06 from 14.98 percent late on Tuesday after the market held above 15 percent during the day.

Economists polled by Reuters forecast credit would rise to 16.40 percent year-on-year from a preliminary 15.96 percent while money supply was seen climbing to 16.70 percent year-on-year from a preliminary 16.39.
"Positions are already squared off for settlement on Thursday and the market is pretty long stock," one dealer commented, also saying that a slightly higher figure could already be discounted.
"But if it is a particularly bad number the market will kick up," he added.
April inflation data, released earlier in the day, elicited a muted response from the bond market although the figure was at the high end of market expectations.
Inflation came in at 0.9 percent month-on-month or 9.9 percent year-on-year against a consensus of 9.6 percent year-on-year and 0.6 percent month-on-month.
Traders said the market was little troubled by the figure as it held below the important 10 percent mark as expected.
Direction was seen dictated by the money supply and credit data with 15.11 percent seen toppish on Thursday even if the numbers were worse-than-expected.
Also due on Thursday morning at 0730 GMT are first quarter GDP growth numbers, the last in a slew of economic releases to hit the market this week.
Seasonally adjusted and annualised quarter-on-quarter GDP at market prices was forecast at 2.5 percent from 3.3 percent in the fourth quarter last year.
Foreigners were net sellers of 458.79 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 47.61 million rand's worth on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal turnover on the exchange was 5.92 billion rand on Tuesday from 4.42 billion rand on Monday.
On the forex market, the rand was stronger in late trade on good exporter dollar supply after importers tried unsuccessfully to ramp the unit higher above the 4.48 level in the morning.
At 1616 GMT the rand was changing hands at 4.4710/4740 on the U.S. dollar from late levels of 4.4775/4805 on Tuesday with Thursday's range put between 4.47 to 4.48.
"The 4.48 level held in the early morning and then at around 0800 GMT a big London bank and exporters sold dollars," a senior trader commented.

He said there had been a fair amount of exports during the day, leading the rand stronger but Thursday would likely see the return of usual week-end dollar demand in order to buy back short positions.
"Dollar demand will probably drive the rand to 4.48 and I expect exporters to step in at that level again," the dealer added.
In cross rate action, the rand was last changing hands at 0.3790/3793 to the mark from 0.3798/3802 late on Tuesday.
The local unit was trading at 25.7909/8194 yen from 26.0106/0392 yen previously and 7.3233/3327 rand to the British pound from 7.2892/2986 before.
South Africa's money market shortage fell to 6.780 billion rand on Tuesday from 7.599 billion rand on Monday, the Reserve Bank said.
Three-month NCD rates remained unchanged from Friday at 16.35 percent offered, as did 90-day BA rates which lined up at 15.85 percent.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482-1003
